evidence: task/instruction.md is three first-person prose paragraphs (lines 1,3,5): a motivation ('I often paste a long one-line experiment, format it, make changes in several places, and then run it beside the source'), a pointer to the six notes and seed, and a short runtime/handover paragraph ('I start it with node /app/server.js ... check it yourself the way I'll use it'). Against the quality-checks.md line 11 defect list: grep for must/shall, bullet markers, numbered items and table pipes over instruction.md and all six notes found none except one in-prose 'must not' (behaviour.md:13); there is no feature matrix, no acceptance checklist, and no build recipe - framework, frontend tools, routes and schema are explicitly left open (integration.md:5, policy.md:3). The fixed paths (/app, /app/server.js, /app/app.db, port 3000, DB_PATH, /api/health) are the template runtime contract owned by check 4, stated once in user voice. Notes stay in the same voice with use-case rationales (ui.md:7 'I often have one very long line', behaviour.md:9 'I sometimes have the same revision open in two tabs'). Residual observation, not a defect for this row: ui.md and behaviour.md are dense and enumerate many edge cases (e.g. ui.md:7 Tab outdent boundary, ui.md:11 replace-contains-search, behaviour.md:13 network-panel/idempotent-restore rationale), so they read like a demanding developer's wishlist bordering on acceptance criteria in prose; the 'SQLite' mandate (integration.md:9) is a technology choice whose fairness belongs to rows 4/6/coverage review. Counterexample search: this is a source-only wording row, so no broken app or conforming alternative changes its outcome; no runtime evidence is required (run_verdict NOT EXERCISED is accurate). Template files are CHANGE_ME placeholders and task-authored, so no template-controlled wording conflict.
